brief_corrections.claim_in_brief: Budget exhaustion alone is harmless; budget exhaustion while the store is refusing writes silences the agent. P(answer | budget>0) = 1.000 at every level.
brief_corrections.correction: True but conditioned on the wrong variable, and the 'budget>0' cell is confounded with turn position. The discriminator is the REFUSAL. Splitting the same v3 turns by whether the turn contained a memory-full result: P(answer | b=0, no refusal) = 0.990 (n=195) at n=2 and 0.993 (n=276) at n=3, indistinguishable from n=1's 0.974 (n=347); P(answer | b=0, refusal) = 0.174 (n=363) and 0.134 (n=374). n=1 is the position control: its zero-budget turns ARE late turns and they answer.
brief_corrections.why_it_matters: It changes what iteration 5 must predict. 'zero_budget_share collapses' would FAIL on a working mechanism, because demand stays at ~1.5 calls/turn. The falsifiable form is memory_full == 0.00 plus P(answer | b=0) >= 0.97.

brief_corrections.claim_in_brief: on v3's budget-available turns the model answered 100% of the time, yet n=2 answered is only 7.98 of 14 -- so where do the other ~6 turns go?
brief_corrections.correction: Into one alternating half of the block. The per-turn answer rate at n=3 is EXACTLY 0.00 on every even turn from turn 6 on, over 50 blocks at temperature 0, and 0.66-1.00 on every odd turn. At n=2 the rates over the 14 scored turns are 1.00 0.92 0.86 0.24 0.72 0.16 0.68 0.20 0.74 0.32 0.76 0.26 0.80 0.30, which sum to 7.96 against the reported answered of 7.98. Fully accounted.
brief_corrections.mechanism_of_the_period: The refused delete_key repair is emitted as TEXT, so it never executes, so the store is still full two turns later. The failure regenerates its own precondition, which is why it is periodic rather than diffuse.

brief_corrections.claim_in_brief: `episodic_primacy` is direct evidence that you cannot assume the two fixes compose (EVICTS + v2's step() gave n=3 3.90).
brief_corrections.correction: episodic_primacy did not contain primacy's rule. PrimacyMemory._episode_mark() / PrimacyV2Memory._episode_mark() count role=='user' messages in owner._messages, which is 1 on EVERY turn under a step() that calls reset_messages(), so the mark never changes and _sync_episode() never advances: every write in a block lands in one episode and residents accrue unbounded rehearsal credit. Replaying the real n-back write sequences through PrimacyMemory with an advancing mark vs a frozen one: final key sets differ on 18 of 50 blocks at n=2 and 17 of 50 at n=3; evictions 246 -> 155 and 329 -> 201.
brief_corrections.the_comment_is_backwards: The source comment reads 'Monotonic, so CLEARING the message history advances the episode rather than colliding with an earlier one. This is what makes the candidate safe to compose with a reset_messages() rewrite.' Monotonicity prevents a collision with an earlier episode; it does nothing about a mark that never moves.
brief_corrections.why_it_matters: episodic_primacy's nback 0.5893 measures an untested third store, so it is weaker evidence against composition than the brief treats it as. This candidate reads the presentation boundary from len(_step_log), which v3 already uses and which is invariant to history clearing.

brief_corrections.claim_in_brief: Run-to-run noise is measured twice and is task-dependent: craft 0.0000-0.0031, word_recognition 0.0000, digit_span_reverse 0.0000, story 0.0012, ... 8-task mean 0.0001.
brief_corrections.correction: Those figures understate the spread on the batch tasks, and v3's own run proves it. v3 overrides only step(); encode() calls step() exactly once, _episode_turn_index() is therefore 1 so no control-state block is prepended, and recall() never calls step() -- so the six encode()->recall() tasks run a code path that is PROVABLY IDENTICAL to the baseline's. On that identical path craft_task moved 0.0248 (0.8907 -> 0.8659) and word_recognition moved +0.0460 (0.4948 -> 0.5408). Recorded craft noise is 0.0031, understated by 8x.
brief_corrections.second_line_of_evidence: primacy and primacy_v2 were established in iteration 3 to be the same harness (zero divergences over 874 rows and 3610 write calls). Their semantic_story_recall runs end with DIFFERENT stores on 200 of 200 rows, narrative_qa on 27 of 50, word_recognition on 37 of 50, craft_task on 5 of 150. The serving stack is not deterministic at temperature 0 on a batch encode.
brief_corrections.why_it_matters: The brief requires a no-change control on the six batch tasks with per-task bands from the measured noise table. Banded that way the row fails for nondeterminism and, by pre-registration, voids everything below it -- which is exactly how two candidates already lost creditable gains. P8 bands from the identical-path deltas instead, and references v3 rather than the baseline.

brief_corrections.claim_in_brief: (implicit in the brief and in iteration 4) n=1 is fixed under v3.
brief_corrections.correction: True of answered (13.98) and of zero silent rows, NOT of accuracy. v3's n=1 acc_over_answered is 0.8497 against the baseline's 0.9943, with keys_held 1.00 -> 2.06 and memory_full still 0.00 per turn over 750 turns. Not an overflow effect: rendering the store into the prompt every turn changed the n=1 strategy from one overwritten key to two.
brief_corrections.why_it_matters: P1's n=1 accuracy leg must be pitched at 0.8497, not 0.9943, or the precondition fails on an inherited cost of the parent.

brief_corrections.claim_in_brief: So iteration 5 is ONE change, not two: remove the refusal. ... an evicting store composed with v3's closed leak should clear the n-back floor without any further prompt work.
brief_corrections.correction: The prompt part is right -- the prompt delta here is zero characters. The store part is not: an UNCONDITIONAL evicting store is measured to trade the nback violation for another one. displacement (LRU) semantic_story_recall -0.0509 against a 0.030 floor; primacy (ACT-R) craft_task -0.0451 and narrative_qa -0.0309. And on craft the cause is not the victim order -- mean keys held goes 3.33 refusing -> 3.67 under EITHER rule, because a refusing store makes the agent burn calls on repairs that tool_calls[:remaining] truncates, so it ends holding fewer chunks. Admitting those writes hands a batch task more retained material and the objective inverts.
brief_corrections.consequence: The change is one rule but it is regime-conditional: displacement ACROSS presentations, selection cap WITHIN one. See MANIFEST.md section 2 for the account and section 3 for why that is not a dodge.

diagnosis.cause_A: v2's control-state block carried the maintenance obligation across the turn boundary and dropped the response obligation. Fixed by v3's third sentence: n=3 answered 2.12 -> 7.44, variable_mapping unparsed 38 -> 0. A CEILING on the answer rate, not an addend -- which is why episodic_primacy, which fixed only B, reached 3.90.
diagnosis.cause_B: a write to a new key on a full store is refused; the refused call still consumes a tool call (_tool_calls_used increments regardless of the result); that exhausts a budget of max(6, 1.5*interactions) against a demand of 1.47-1.48 calls/turn; step() then switches to tool_choice='none'; the model emits its delete_key repair as PLAIN TEXT instead of the answer; the trial scores unanswered AND the delete never executes, so the store is still full two turns later. Period 2. Not reachable by any instruction.
diagnosis.why_the_cap_must_not_be_touched: Measured, not judged: on the 471 v3 turns where the budget was exhausted and nothing was refused, the agent answered 99.1% of the time (0.990 at n=2 over 195 turns, 0.993 at n=3 over 276). The budget is not the binding constraint on the failing cell, so raising it buys nothing there while risking the capacity-bound variable_mapping errors that carry the headline.

mechanism.one_sentence: A write to a new key on a full store displaces the least recently refreshed resident laid down in an EARLIER presentation, and is refused with the baseline's exact message when every resident belongs to the CURRENT presentation; a presentation is one step() call, read from len(owner._step_log).
mechanism.prompt_delta: zero characters -- every string and step() itself are episodic_reset_v3's, character for character
citations: Cowan 2001 -- focus of attention, ~4 chunks, a new chunk enters and the least active leaves
Oberauer & Kliegl 2006; Oberauer, Farrell, Jarrold & Lewandowsky 2016 -- overflow as overwriting, not rejection
Ecker, Lewandowsky & Oberauer 2014 -- removal as an operation in updating

Pollack, Johnson & Knaff 1959; Bunting, Cowan & Saults 2006 -- running-memory span shows recency WITHOUT primacy, which is why the victim is least-recently-refreshed and no activation machinery is used

Miller 1956; Cowan 2001 -- within one presentation the limit is on how many chunks may be carried forward, i.e. selection, which is the only reading under which the baseline's error string is admissible
mechanism.no_swept_constants: there is no numeric parameter of any kind in this candidate: no decay, no rate, no threshold, no RNG

P(answer|b=0) = among turns with tool_call_budget_after == 0, the share whose `text`, AFTER stripping <tool_call>...</tool_call> blocks, parses under bench.tasks.wm_nback._parse_classification. displacement = share of turns with a result containing 'was displaced and is now lost'.

offline_stub_reference.note: the real run_nback_block driven by a stub reproducing the model's observed strategy and its observed failure; 1 block per level, so these are mechanism demonstrations, not level models

predictions.threshold_derivation: A refusal IS still reachable under this rule -- it needs four residents all laid down in the CURRENT turn plus a fifth write in that same turn, which turn 1 permits because the budget is 6 and the store is empty, and v3's own calls-per-turn histogram already shows one 4-call turn at n=2 ({1:464, 2:291, 3:44, 4:1}). So an absolute zero would be one legitimate event away from failing with the mechanism working -- the same mis-scaling the WORKLOG records for iteration 4's 'at most 2 turns' contamination bar. The bar is therefore a RATE of 0.01 per turn, and the sharper leg is qualitative: EVERY memory-full event must be one where all four residents were written in that same turn, which is readable straight from step_log[*].tool_calls. This keeps all the instrument-integrity power, because a non-advancing presentation mark produces ~0.47 per turn -- 47x the bar, not one event over it. The 0.97 leg is n=1's own measured 0.974, the level at which an exhausted budget is demonstrably harmless.
predictions.disconfirm_if: memory_full exceeds 0.01 per turn at any level, or any memory-full event is one where a resident from an EARLIER turn was present, or P(answer | b=0) is below 0.97 at any level. The first two say the rule did not engage; the third says the diagnosis in brief_corrections C1 is wrong and the budget really was the binding constraint after all.
predictions.role: primary -- this is the row that separates 'the fix engaged' from 'the score moved'
predictions.capable_of_varying: memory_full took 0.00/0.4775/0.4682 in the one run where it is measurable, and P(answer|b=0) took 0.9741/0.4588/0.4985 in the same run.
predictions.note: zero_budget_share is REPORTED AND NOT PREDICTED, against the brief's instruction, and this is deliberate: n=1 is the control and it says an exhausted budget is harmless (share 0.4627, answers 0.9741, zero refusals). Under this rule the agent still wants ~1.5 writes per turn against 1.5 granted, and in the offline stub drive the budget stays pinned at zero on 12/13/14 turns while answered goes to 14/14/14. Predicting a collapse would fail the row while the mechanism worked.

predictions.name: variable_mapping holds up, raw and matched, with its error structure intact
predictions.direction_stated_in_advance: a small FALL from v3's 0.6767 is expected and accepted. Under v3 the store FREEZES on the first four names -- it changes on only 211 of 1350 consecutive-question transitions -- and accuracy is 0.9833 when the queried name is resident against 0.2561 when it is not. Replacing the freeze with displacement changes WHICH names are resident. Replaying the run's own records, the queried name is resident on 840/1500 questions under v3, 827/1500 under LRU-over-names and 821/1500 under an ACT-R top-4, so the residency RATE moves by about 1%; if LRU residency carried v3's conditional accuracies, vm accuracy would go 0.6633 -> 0.6391.
predictions.disconfirm_if: raw below 0.55 or matched below 0.60 (the freeze, not the leak closure, was carrying the gain), or n_errors below 150 (the errors evaporated), or rc_ratio_normalized outside [0.15, 0.95] (the errors stopped being interference-shaped).
predictions.bound_not_forecast: every residency figure above replays the write sequence the model produced under a REFUSING store. Under eviction it will not emit the delete-as-text repair and will spend the freed budget differently.
predictions.note: The interference structure A4 measures is robust to the overflow rule: mean relation_count among non-residents over residents is 1.374 (v3), 1.388 (LRU), 1.393 (ACT-R top-4), against a human 1.386.
